```markdown # DESIGN.md: The Bayes Group marketing site (prerendered static, redesign) ## Users and goal **Users:** owners, general managers and operations leads at small and medium-sized businesses (10–500 people) who are weighing outside help with AI. A second group is enterprise leaders who need a senior, governed partner. They arrive from referrals, search or a shared link, often on a phone between meetings, and they are wary of hype. **The one job:** decide within a minute that this is an established, credible firm that fits a business their size, then book a consultation. **Success feels like:** "These are senior experts who work with companies like mine, and they will leave my team owning the result." Pages look complete and polished on first paint, shared links show a real title and description, and the message sends with a clear confirmation. ## Primary flow 1. Land on Home (`/`). The prerendered hero shows the h1, the value proposition and **Book a consultation**. 2. Press **Book a consultation**. It is in the hero, the header (desktop), the open Menu (phone) and the closing CTA band, and it goes to `/contact`. The page scrolls to the top and focus moves to `
`. 3. Fill in **Name**, **Email** and **Message**. **Company**, **Company size** and **What can we help with?** are optional. 4. Press **Send message**. The site shows "Thanks, we'll be in touch within one business day." and clears the form. **Secondary paths** - Home → **See engagements** or **Enterprise engagements** → `/engagements` (or `#enterprise`) → a tier's **Book a consultation** or **Talk to us about enterprise** → `/contact`. - Home → **Explore services** or a pillar's **Learn more** → the matching `/services` section, scrolled below the sticky header. The header CTA and the footer nav are on every page, so no page is a dead end. ## Screens and states The site is static, so nothing loads and no page shows a spinner. Every page is a full HTML file that React hydrates. Long words and the email address use `overflow-wrap: anywhere`. Photos reserve their space with width and height and sit on a navy (`#0B1F3A`) background, so a slow image never shifts the layout or leaves white text on white. **Page metadata.** Each file has one title, one description, og tags, a canonical link and the favicon. | Path | Title | Description | |---|---|---| | / | The Bayes Group \| Evidence-driven AI | Evidence-driven AI consulting, training and custom development led by two credentialed data scientists. | | /services | Services \| The Bayes Group | AI enablement, team training and custom AI development that deliver measurable results for your business. | | /training | Training \| The Bayes Group | Practical AI courses for executives, managers and technical teams, taught by working data scientists. | | /engagements | Engagements \| The Bayes Group | Right-sized AI engagements for small and medium-sized businesses, with a premium tier for enterprise. | | /about | About \| The Bayes Group | Meet the data scientists behind The Bayes Group and the values that guide our work. | | /contact | Contact \| The Bayes Group | Book a consultation with The Bayes Group and get a reply within one business day. | | 404 | Page not found \| The Bayes Group | The page you requested could not be found on The Bayes Group website. | **Navigation states** - **First load:** no scroll and no focus change. - **Later route change:** the window scrolls to (0,0) and focus moves to `
`. - **Route change with a hash:** the page scrolls to the target, which has `scroll-margin-top: 96px`. - **Header:** on top it is white with no border. Once `scrollY > 8`, the class `is-scrolled` adds a 1px `#DCE3EB` bottom border. The current link has `aria-current="page"` and a 2px teal underline. **Home:** sections in this order: 1. Hero 2. Credibility strip 3. Who we serve 4. What we do 5. How we work 6. Client results 7. Testimonial 8. Why The Bayes Group 9. CTA band **Placeholder content (Home and About)** - Each case-study card shows an amber **Placeholder** tag and the italic note "Placeholder case study: replace with a real client engagement before launch." - The testimonial shows the note "Placeholder testimonial: replace with a real client quote before launch." **Engagements:** a page header (h1, intro), then four tier cards, then the "Not sure which fits?" line. - Enterprise is the premium card and spans the full width below the three business tiers. - Many list items: the lists grow and the cards in a row keep equal height, with buttons pinned to the bottom. **Services:** a page header, then three sections (`enablement`, `training`, `custom-development`). Each section has a photo header, item cards with icons, and the "Typical engagement: …" line. **Training** - **Default:** "All" is pressed and the count reads "Showing 6 courses" (`role="status"`). - **Filtered:** for example, "Showing 2 courses for Managers". - **Empty:** "No courses for this audience yet." with **Show all courses**. **About:** mission and Why Bayes beside the photo, two founder cards, four values. - Each founder card has an avatar silhouette with the caption "Photo placeholder", the **Placeholder** tag and the note "Placeholder: replace with founder credentials and bio." **Contact** - **Default:** empty fields. Name, Email and Message each show a "Required" tag. - **Error:** shown on blur for a field you have touched and for all fields on submit. Focus moves to the first invalid field. Messages: - "Please enter your name." - "Please enter a valid email address." - "Please enter a message." - **Optional fields:** Company, Company size and topic never show an error. - **Success:** a green banner with `role="status"` and `tabIndex=-1` that receives focus and reads "Thanks, we'll be in touch within one business day." The form clears. The banner hides on the next edit. - **Loading:** none. Submit is synchronous and the button is never disabled. **Not found:** a small bell-curve illustration, the h1 "Page not found", the text "The page you're looking for doesn't exist or has moved.", then **Back to home** and **View services**. ## Layout **Global** - Container max-width 1200px, centered. Side padding is 24px on phones and 40px at ≥1024px. - `html, body { overflow-x: hidden }`. `img, svg { max-width: 100%; height: auto }`. - Breakpoints: phone below 768px, tablet 768–1023px, desktop ≥1024px. The header shows the five links only at ≥1024px; below that it uses the Menu button. - Header: 72px tall, `position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 50`. - Section rhythm: 64px top and bottom on phones, 112px on desktop. message.content:
All 313 acceptance tests pass and the build, `tsc`, accessibility, phone-layout and prerender checks pass. One check still fails: "ui primary flow".

**The failing check.** Step 3 of the read-only `ui_flow.json` expects the old value proposition, "We help your team find, build and own AI…". The next step expects the new one, and the task requires the new one. Both can't be on Home at once, so I reported step 3 with `dispute_test` rather than keep the old copy. The flow can't get past step 3, so its later steps haven't run.

**What I changed**
- **Head and routing:**
  - `/engagements` is now in `src/seo.ts` with its title and description.
  - `getPageTitle` in `src/content/site.ts` returns the Engagements title.
  - `scripts/prerender.mjs` prerenders the page, and `public/sitemap.xml` lists six pages.
- **Docs:** `DEPLOYMENT.md` lists `dist/engagements/index.html`, says images are in `dist/images`, and says six pages.
- **Icons and illustrations:**
  - `Icons.tsx` has a 24px line-icon set (1.5px stroke) with one icon per service item, training format, tier, value and credibility point.
  - `Illustrations.tsx` has the bell-curve motif, data-grid pattern, avatar silhouette and not-found illustration.
- **Pages:**
  - **Home:** reworked with the hero overlay, credibility strip, who-we-serve panels, pillar photos, case studies, testimonial, why-us photo and CTA band.
  - **Engagements:** a new page with four tier cards and a premium Enterprise card.
  - **Services, Training, About, Contact, Not found:** all updated as the task describes.
- **Header and footer:**
  - The header adds an `is-scrolled` class once the page scrolls.
  - The footer now has Services and Company columns plus the email.
- **Contact form:** `COMPANY_SIZE_OPTIONS` and `companySize` are added.
- **Styles:**
  - I rewrote `theme.css`, `global.css` and `tokens.ts` with the navy/teal tokens, the display size, hover lifts, CSS-only fade-in, navy gradient overlays, and the reduced-motion block (animation, transition and transform off).
  - Photos stay in the markup with srcset, sizes, width/height and lazy loading (except the hero), per the task.

I also added an "h2 What we do" heading to the pillars section and the line "Tell us about your goals. We'll reply within one business day." to the CTA band, because `ui_flow.json` expects both.

I didn't update `DESIGN.md`, and I didn't touch `ui_flow.json`, which is read-only.

I changed no code this round. The one failing check can only be fixed in `ui_flow.json`, which I'm not allowed to edit.

- **The conflict:** step 3 of `ui_flow.json` expects the old hero line, "We help your team find, build and own AI that delivers measurable results, guided by two credentialed data scientists." The hero shows only one value proposition, so both steps can't pass.
- **What I did:** I filed a `dispute_test` quoting both steps and asking for the stale step 3 to be removed. The hero keeps the new text, so I haven't bent the site to the old step.
- **Rest of the flow:** I searched the source for the strings the other steps expect that I wasn't sure of. All are present, for example "Client name, Title, Company" and "Tell us about your business". I haven't run the full flow past step 3, because it stops at the failure, so those later steps are untested.
- **Tests:** the last full acceptance run passed (313 tests across 30 suites). I didn't re-run the tests or the validate tool this round, since nothing changed.

message.content:
I made one real fix, to the hero heading size on phones. The other listed items are already in the code, and I didn't change them. The 313 acceptance tests and every `validate` check still pass. The only failure is a non-blocking Trivy warning about two react-router vulnerabilities, which can't be fixed from the app. I didn't look at new screenshots, so the phone and desktop results below are unchecked.

- **Hero h1 too large on phones (R16):** The hero h1 is now 36px (2.25rem) below 768px, set in `src/styles/global.css`. I also stated the display size explicitly in the 1024px+ rule. Desktop still uses the 60px `--text-display` token.
- **Headings not serif (R13):** The CSS already sets `font-family: var(--font-serif)` on all headings. The phone screenshots from the last round show the h1 and the credibility-strip titles in serif. I made no change here.
- **Reviewer notes on the footer "Company" heading and the Placeholder tags and notes:** The code already has them, so there was nothing to fix. The footer has a "Company" column title. Each case-study card has the "Placeholder" tag and note. The testimonial has its note. The tests pass with these in place.
- **Remaining items (R35, R59–R64, R86, R90, R134, R159, R168):** The components for these exist and the UI flow walks through them. The screenshot comments describe a cropped phone viewport, not missing markup:
  - Who we serve (R59–R64) is a stacked phone layout that becomes side by side from 1024px.
  - The contact two-column layout (R159) is likewise desktop only.
  - Testimonial, Why Bayes and footer (R86, R90, R168) sit below the screenshot crop.
  - Training format icons (R35) are rendered on every course card.
  - Services (R134) has a photo in each section header.

I made no code changes this round. I found nothing in the source that needs fixing, and all 313 acceptance tests and every `validate` check pass.

- **Reviewer notes:** the three open notes from the reviewer are already satisfied in the current code.
  - The footer has a "Company" column title and the nav has `aria-label="Footer"`.
  - Each case-study card renders the "Placeholder" tag and `CASE_STUDY_NOTE`.
  - The testimonial block renders its note and attribution.
- **R13 (serif headings):** the h1, the h2s and the credibility-point titles all use `var(--font-serif)`. The screenshot also shows serif letterforms.
- **R16 (hero h1 size):** on phones the hero h1 is 2.25rem, which is 36px. The screenshot is 2x, and its 85px line spacing is 36px × 1.2 line height at 2x.
- **R60, R61, R86, R90, R134, R159, R168, R35:** these flagged screens all fail for the same reason.
  - Every one of the screenshots, including the contact, services, training and footer screens, shows the top of the Home page at 390×844.
  - The audit therefore never saw the sections it checked.
  - The code already has these sections:
    - Home has the stacked "Who we serve" panels with the `smb-owner` and `enterprise-atrium` photos, the navy testimonial, and "Why The Bayes Group" beside the `about-office` photo.
    - Services has the photo section headers.
    - Contact has the two-column grid at ≥1024px.
    - The footer is navy with columns at ≥1024px.
    - Training cards have format icons.
- **Not fixed:** I didn't change `ui_flow.json`, so the screenshots will keep showing the top of the page and the audit will keep misjudging those screens. Phone view, where everything is one column, is the case I'd most want a person to check by eye.

I made no code changes this round. The files already contain the fixes for the listed problems, and the screenshots don't show them.

The phone screenshots are all the same view of the top of Home: header, hero and the start of the credibility strip. Nothing below that was captured. Several of the unmet requirements (R60, R61, R86, R90, R134, R159, R168) are about sections that sit lower on the page or on other screens, so the reviewer could not have seen them.

What the code and the screenshots show for each flagged item:
- **R13, serif headings:** `global.css` sets `font-family: var(--font-serif)` on all headings, and the hero h1 and strip titles render in a serif face in the screenshot.
- **R16, phone hero h1:** the phone rule is `.hero h1 { font-size: 2.25rem }`, which is 36px and inside the required 36–40px. The screenshot is at 2× scale, so it looks larger than it is.
- **R35 and R134:** `TrainingPage.tsx` and `ServicesPage.tsx` already have the training format icons and the Services section header (`.service-header`, with the strategy-session photo).
- **R159 and R168:** `.contact-grid` is a 7fr/5fr split from 1024px, and the footer is navy. Both are desktop layouts, and these screenshots are 390px phones.
- **R60, R61, R86 and R90:** I did not look at the Who we serve, testimonial or Why The Bayes Group markup this round. The tests cover these sections and pass.
- **Reviewer's list of missing items:** the Engagements page, `engagements.ts`, the nav links, the footer links, the Company size select, the placeholder tags and notes, and the reduced-motion media query are all present in the files list or in the code I read. The reviewer attached no failing reproduction to any of them.

I did not re-run `run_tests` this round. The last full run, in the task statement, had 30 suites and 313 tests passing. The `validate` run I did this round passed every blocking check: build, UI render, UI styles, accessibility, phone layout, UI primary flow, prerendered pages, tsc and the security scanners. The only failing check is non-blocking: two medium react-router CVEs that can't be fixed from the app.

However we need to verify all listed requirements are indeed implemented. Many requirements were recorded as R###. The tests are relatively thorough. But there might be missing requirements not covered by tests. The validator shows static validation passed (everything builds). Now we need to verify requirements.

We have to list missing_requirements (IDs for requirements not implemented), and wrong_tests (if any failing test is wrong). The acceptance tests passed all tests: 30 passed for acceptance, static checks passed except trivy warnings about react-router CVEs. That's okay: not a requirement.

Now need to examine each requirement ID: R2 through R173 etc. Let's list them and see if code implements.

Better approach: go through each R ID and search code for features. However the acceptance tests that cover many of them presumably verify.

But we must double-check completeness: For example, R8: Menu button works after hydration. The hydration tests include test for menu button after hydration. That passes.

R7: training filter works after hydration, test passes.

R9: contact form works after hydration, test passes.

R13,14: headings serif, body sans-serif: CSS defines h1-h6 fonts: var(--font-serif); body uses var(--font-sans). Good.

R15,16: hero h1 display size about 56-64px on desktop (~60px), 36-40px on phones (~40?). CSS: .hero h1 uses var(--text-display). In theme.css, var(--text-display) is 2.5rem on mobile (2.5rem = 40px; assuming root font = 16px => 40px). At min-width:1024, var(--text-display): 3.75rem = 60px. Good.

R18: cards have soft shadows: CSS card has var(--shadow-card) and hover uses var(--shadow-card-hover). Soft shadows. Good.

R19: cards lift slightly on hover: translateY(-4px). Good.

R20: sections fade/slide in subtle, no other motion beyond hover. CSS includes .fade-in animation; however need to check sections have class .fade-in or .reveal? In global.css: .fade-in { animation: fade-up 600ms ease-out; }. Many components may have reveal class? Not seeing. There is .hero etc. Possibly sections have class .section with .fade-in? Might be defined elsewhere in component code. Need to inspect if sections have these classes. Let's open HomePage component for sections.

message.content:
I made one change this round, a phone-only fix to the hero in `src/styles/global.css`. It addresses the R16 finding (hero h1 too large on phones). The other open requirements (R60, R61, R86, R90, R159 and R168) are not fixed, because I found nothing in the code to change for them.

- **What I changed (R16):** On screens under 768px the hero is now tighter. The h1 is 2.25rem (36px) with a 14ch width cap that no longer applies. The hero's minimum height is removed, and its padding and button spacing are smaller. The lead paragraph is slightly smaller, and the credibility strip is more compact. This should bring the "Who we serve" panels and the rest of the page closer to the top of the screen. I haven't looked at a new phone screenshot to confirm it.
- **What I did not change:** The code already has the sections behind the other findings. These are the "Who we serve" panels, the testimonial, "Why The Bayes Group", the two-column Contact layout, and the navy multi-column footer. The CSS also already has the footer styling and the two-column desktop contact grid. The failing screenshots all show the same top-of-page view, so those items were probably just off-screen when captured. I didn't confirm that.
- **Reviewer notes:** Most reviewer open notes describe things that already exist, such as the Engagements page, the "Company size" field and the reduced-motion media query. I left those alone.
- **Checks:** All 313 acceptance tests pass. `validate` passes, including the build, prerender, accessibility, phone layout and UI flow checks. The one non-blocking trivy warning (react-router 6.30.6, two medium CVEs) can't be fixed from the app.

I made no changes this round, because the open items look like a screenshot problem rather than a code problem.

All 313 acceptance tests and every `validate` check pass, including the render, styles, accessibility, phone-layout and UI-flow checks. The only non-blocking item is two MEDIUM `react-router` advisories that can't be fixed from the app.

- **Same image every time:** the phone screenshots for every step of the flow are the same top-of-home frame. The hero and the 2×2 credibility strip are in view, and nothing else ever scrolls into the capture. The reviewer's complaints all fit that:
  - **Who we serve, testimonial, Why The Bayes Group, contact two-column, footer:** the reviewer says these are missing, but each is built and in the DOM. They were never in frame.
  - **Who we serve:** the reviewer read the credibility strip as the "Who we serve" panels. That strip is a 2×2 grid on phones, so it looked like a single four-feature panel.
  - **Serif headings:** in the screenshot the h1 and the wordmark are rendered in serif. `global.css` sets `--font-serif` on h1–h6, the wordmark, the credibility items and the step numerals.
- **Not fixable on my side:** `ui_flow.json` is off-limits to me, so I couldn't change how the flow captures each screen. I didn't change the layout or the markup to chase a frame that doesn't show the sections.
- **Code confirmation, no change made:**
